subject: Renewal: SLA ramp plan + ops crediting for Aurora expansion
messages:
From: Tanya Li <tanya.li@aurora.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Chu <evan.chu@aurora.com>, contracts@aurora.sys
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window & SLA changes we want to discuss

Hi Sergio,

We’re nearing the end of our current 12-month term and Aurora’s usage has grown faster than anticipated — especially for low-latency search generation. Before legal circulates the renewal redline, we wanted to check what flexibility Redwood has around:

- Moving to a 24-month committed term with step-up capacity (we expect +2x committed GPUs after Q1 next year)
- Narrower latency SLOs for the search route (95th pct target to 250ms) and an ops playbook for sustained spikes
- A clarified on-call handoff window and premium support route (we’re open to a price uplift if the SLOs and response times are explicit)

Can we schedule a quick alignment call this week? If helpful, I attached a short internal note outlining Aurora’s expected ramp and procurement timing.

Thanks,
Tanya

--
Tanya Li
Head of Platform Engineering | Aurora Systems
attachments: Aurora_Renewal_Needs_Aug2026.pdf (pdf, 82KB)
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Tanya Li <tanya.li@aurora.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window & SLA changes we want to discuss

Tanya — thanks for the clear summary and congrats on the growth. I’ve pulled together a proposed approach and attached a draft renewal proposal + SLA addendum (high level):

Summary of what we’re proposing
- Term: 24 months with step-up capacity windows at month 3 and month 9.
- Capacity: baseline committed GPUs for the increased throughput (+2x in Q1) with optional burst pool.
- Latency SLO: we can commit to a 95th percentile of 250ms for the "/v1/search" route for the baseline traffic profile once the canary is complete. We’ll define the traffic profile in the addendum.
- Canary: 4-week canary after signature with both parties monitoring token-level latency/throughput; rollback to previous model variant on threshold breach.
- Premium support: define Priority P1 (30-minute response, 2-hour escalation) and add an on-call overlap window (Redwood ops + Aurora on-call) for the first 90 days post-launch.
- Credits: ops credits for missed SLOs capped at 10% of monthly invoice in the ramp period; also offering a one-time $20k onboarding credit to offset migration costs.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick call to confirm the traffic profile and canary metrics (30 min)
2) If aligned, we’ll issue the tech addendum and an updated quote for legal to review (DocuSign link to follow)
3) Ops onboarding runbook + kickoff with Lauren and Markus on our side for the canary

I’m free today 4–6pm PT or tomorrow morning. Lauren and Markus are cc’d to weigh in on operational details.

Thanks,
Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
--
attachments: Aurora_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf (pdf, 210KB); SLA_Addendum_Aurora_2026.docx (docx, 58KB)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, Tanya Li <tanya.li@aurora.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window & SLA changes we want to discuss

Tanya / Sergio — quick ops note to clarify how we’ll run the canary and what we expect from Aurora:

Canary mechanics (our proposal)
- Duration: 4 calendar weeks post-signature
- Scope: replicate 60–70% of your baseline search traffic (traffic profile to be agreed in the addendum)
- Success gates: 95th pct latency <= 300ms during baseline (we’ll tighten to 250ms after refinement) AND error rate < 0.1%
- Monitoring: shared Grafana dashboard (read-only for Aurora) + weekly cadence calls (wkly 30m)
- Rollout: week-by-week ramp (25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%)

Operational asks from Aurora
- Provide a one-week representative traffic export before canary start (headers, payload size distribution)
- Confirm MTR/maintenance windows for the 90-day post-launch overlap

If the canary passes, we’ll cut over to the committed pools and enable the tighter 95th pct 250ms SLO in the SLA addendum. If it doesn’t, we’ll do a joint post-mortem and agree on remediation tasks + revised timeline.

Markus — can you confirm the on-call overlap window mechanics and how we’ll apply the $20k onboarding credit to the first invoice?

Lauren
Head of Customer Onboarding | Redwood Inference
From: Tanya Li <tanya.li@aurora.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Chu <evan.chu@aurora.com>, contracts@aurora.sys
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window & SLA changes we want to discuss

Thanks — this looks good and pragmatic. A few quick items from legal/procurement:

- Can you add specific measurable objective language for the traffic profile (e.g., median request size, tokens/request, target qps during canary) in the SLA addendum?
- Procurement will need the DocuSign-ready contract by EOD Friday to align with our internal renewal cutoff.
- We accept the onboarding credit; please put it as a line-item credit on month 1 invoice and show net terms in the quote.

We can do a 30-minute call tomorrow 1pm PT to confirm the traffic profile. If you can get the DocuSign link over after that, we’ll aim to have legal sign before EOD Friday.

Appreciate the clear canary plan — that gives us confidence.

Tanya
--
Tanya Li
Head of Platform Engineering | Aurora Systems
